Table projection points to wrong database after renaming
When I change the database or table name for a ClickHouse source in direct-query mode and save, the reprojected table still queries the old database. The schema row saves correctly but the live query table is rebuilt against the previous location, so my HogQL queries return data from the wrong place until I manually refresh or re-sync.

Tables with database-prefixed names are silently skipped during sync setup
When a default database is configured for a data source, schema names that include a database prefix are not split into separate database and table components. Instead, the full prefixed name is treated as the table name, causing schema lookups to fail and those tables to be skipped during synchronization.

Placeholders in storage path prefix left unresolved for continuous exports
When a batch export is configured without an end time, placeholders in the storage path prefix are written literally into file paths instead of being resolved. The table name placeholder, for example, appears as raw text in the generated paths rather than the actual table name.

Date placeholders left unresolved in manifest path for unbounded exports
When configuring a batch export without an end bound, the manifest file path retains the original template placeholders instead of substituting actual date values. I expected all template variables in my key prefix to be filled in, even for exports without an end bound.

Disabling sharing does not revoke access
When I disable sharing on a dashboard, the share link still works after a page reload. I expected that toggling sharing off would immediately invalidate access, since the enabled flag should control whether a configuration is considered active.

Tables vanish from the catalog under heavy load
When processing many tables, some tables disappear entirely from the generated catalog even though most of their fields are valid. The issue appears intermittently after adding more tables or when the total number of fields grows large. I expected all serializable tables to appear in the catalog regardless of how many other tables were processed.

Duplicate virtual relations for the same table
When a table can be reached through multiple parent paths in the schema, the catalog output contains duplicate relation definitions for that same table. For example, if table B is reachable from both table A and table C, the catalog generates two separate relations for B instead of one. I expected each table to appear as a single relation regardless of how many paths lead to it.

Parent navigation breaks after crossing a join
When I run a query that goes back to a parent table after crossing a join, the system throws an error about having no parent to navigate to. The same navigation works fine when I don't cross any joins. I expected the system to track parent tables correctly regardless of joins.

Failed data deletion request marked as completed after retry
When a person or property deletion request fails mid-pipeline and I retry from the failed step, the request ends up in completed status even though the underlying deletion never actually succeeded. The failure hook correctly marks it as failed, but the finalization step then overwrites that to completed because it accepts the failed state as a valid input. I expect failed requests to stay failed so I can investigate before re-approving.

HogQL event removal fails with confusing permissions error
When I submit a HogQL-based event deletion request, it immediately fails with an error about "no creator whose query permissions can be enforced." The request was created without a user associated with it — there is no creator at all, not even one lacking permissions. The error message makes it sound like a permissions problem rather than missing data, so I have no idea what to fix. I need to know that the request needs a creator assigned before it can proceed.

HogQL event deletion request never completes
After a HogQL-based event deletion job finishes successfully, the request stays in queued status instead of being marked as completed. It sits there indefinitely even though the events have already been deleted. I expected the request to transition to completed once the job runs.

GitLab file link resolver never finds files
When I use the GitLab file link resolver with a code snippet and file name, it always returns "not found" even though the file clearly exists in the repository. I tried searching for specific Python files across multiple repositories, but no URL was ever returned. I expected the resolver to find matching files and return their URLs.

No Slack alert when all tests pass
After running the ingestion acceptance test suite successfully, I receive nothing in Slack. There's no confirmation that the suite ran or completed — I have to manually check the Temporal UI to verify it actually executed. When tests fail, I get a detailed notification, but for successful runs there's complete silence. I expected at least a brief "all green" message so I know the suite ran without issues.

Red circle shown next to "Failed: 0" in test results notification
When the ingestion acceptance test run has errors but no actual failures, the Slack notification still displays a red circle emoji next to "Failed: 0". Since the red circle typically signals a problem, this is misleading and makes it look like there are failures when there are none.

Timeout notification picks wrong failure class
When several acceptance tests time out at once, the Slack notification reports that an event never appeared even though some of the hung tests were actually waiting for persons. The failure class should reflect the most relevant issue, not just whichever check runs first.

Metric calculation permanently fails on data quality issues that should self-resolve
When an experiment metric fails to calculate due to insufficient or inconsistent data, the system marks it as permanently failed instead of retrying. Subsequent scheduled runs produce the same failure without trying again. I expected the system to retry automatically and succeed once the data quality issue resolves. Manually triggering a new calculation gives the same result.

Experiment metric stuck in failed state after initial insufficient data error
When an experiment metric calculation fails early due to insufficient data, the metric remains permanently marked as failed. Even after enough data has accumulated for the calculation to succeed, the dashboard continues showing the original error instead of updated results.

Backfill job times out before completing
When I trigger a metrics recalculation for a large experiment, the backfill task appears stuck for many minutes and then times out, even though data is clearly still being written in the background. I expected the backfill to complete successfully and show updated results on the experiment dashboard.

Federated join merge produces incorrect results when inner queries reference joined tables
When a query has multiple LEFT JOINs over federated Postgres tables that get merged into one combined join, any nested subqueries inside the aggregated join branches still reference the original join aliases instead of the new merged one. This causes the query to return wrong values or fail at execution time in ClickHouse. I expected all field references throughout the entire query tree to be updated to point to the single merged join alias.

Machine-readable output lacks clean flag count
When I run the audit command, the console shows a breakdown of valid, invalid, and skipped flags. But when I request machine-readable output, the overall status is just a boolean instead of showing the actual count. I can't determine from the machine-readable output how many flags were actually valid.

Session recording sample rate loses its 100% setting after save
When I save my team's session recording sample rate as 100 percent, the stored value disappears. After refreshing, the setting shows as disabled. The value only disappears for 100 percent - other rates like 50 percent are saved and displayed correctly. I expected the 100 percent setting to be saved and displayed correctly.

Cache verification reports false mismatches right after updating a team
When I verify a team's metadata cache immediately after changing its settings, the check reports a data mismatch even though the background cache refresh is still in progress. Running the same verification a short time later shows a clean match. The verification should skip teams that were recently updated instead of flagging stale cache data as a real problem.

Team metadata returns null after a minor DB hiccup
When the database experiences a brief connectivity issue or timeout, subsequent calls to fetch team metadata start returning null instead of the cached data. The cache should fall back gracefully or preserve the existing entry rather than treating transient errors as permanent misses.

2FA status shows enabled for users with passkeys but no active two-factor
The admin panel displays "Enabled" next to passkeys for a user who has verified passkeys set up but hasn't enabled them for two-factor authentication. Clicking the "Send 2FA reset email" button then reports that the user doesn't have 2FA enabled, contradicting the status shown on the page.

Revoking sessions logs out the admin too
When I'm impersonating a user and click to revoke all their sessions, I get logged out too. Every session for that user gets deleted, including the shared session I'm using to impersonate them.

Can't enable passkeys for 2FA on a user who hasn't set one up yet
When I try to turn on the passkeys-for-2FA toggle in the admin panel, I get an error saying the user has no verified passkey. But the user hasn't gone through the passkey setup flow yet, so there's nothing to verify. I expected to be able to enable the setting first and then have the user complete the verification.

Experiment metric events deleted before 7-day retention period
Preaggregated experiment data disappears after only a few days instead of the documented 7-day retention window. I ran an experiment and noticed that event data from the first couple of days was gone when I tried to analyze results. The expiration logic calculates the cutoff date at midnight rather than using the actual insertion time, so rows inserted later in the day get deleted sooner than expected.

Truncate command fails on preaggregated experiment table
When I run the truncate operation to clean up the preaggregated experiment metric events, it fails with an access denied error. I can query and read from the table without issue, but the truncate refuses to execute. I expected the truncate to work on the same table I use for queries.

Disabled alerts still count toward my plan's alert limit
I turned off three alerts I no longer need, but when I try to create a new one the system says my team has reached its limit. The disabled alerts shouldn't be counting against the quota since they're not active.

Equal threshold bounds are accepted
When I set both the lower and upper thresholds to the same value, the system saves the configuration without any warning. I expected it to reject equal bounds since a range with matching minimum and maximum does not define a meaningful window.

Duplicate notification emails sent to same user
When an alert fires, some users receive multiple identical notification emails even though they only subscribed once. I noticed this after setting up a daily threshold alert — one teammate got three copies of the same notification.

Activity events are not being logged after restart
After restarting the application, I noticed that user activity events stopped being recorded. The feature worked fine before the restart. I expected all activity signals to be captured automatically without needing any manual setup.

Order expression parser doesn't reject empty input
When I pass an empty string to the expression parser, it raises a clear "empty query" error, but the same call to the order expression parser crashes with a confusing low-level parse failure instead. I expected both functions to validate empty input the same way.

Parse errors for template strings report positions shifted two characters ahead
When a template body fails to parse, the error points to a position that is two characters ahead of where the actual problem is in my input. I had to mentally subtract two from every position the parser reported before I could find the issue. Other parsers like the expression and select parsers report correct positions, so this only happens with template parsing.

Empty SELECT statements produce a confusing error instead of a clear message
When I try to parse an empty SELECT statement, I get a low-level error from the parser engine that doesn't explain what went wrong. Parsing other types of expressions gives a straightforward message about empty input, but this one just bubbles up a cryptic failure.

ANY JOIN on persons table returns duplicate rows
When I use a LEFT ANY JOIN on the persons table joined by id, the query returns duplicate rows even though ANY JOIN semantics should only return one match per left row. Other tables get proper deduplication, but the persons table does not.

Severity rule stays disabled after editing severity level
When I change the severity on a rule that had been previously disabled, the rule still appears disabled in the interface. I expected any edit to the rule to reset its disabled state.

Grouping rule assignee can't be changed after creation
I created a grouping rule and assigned it to a team member, but when I tried to edit the rule later the assignee field was locked and I couldn't change it. I had to delete and recreate the rule to reassign it.

Rollout percentage decimal limit ignored for values ending in zero
When I set a rollout percentage to 50.000 it is accepted even though the documentation says at most two decimal places are allowed. A value like 99.900 also slips through, but 99.999 is correctly rejected. It seems like trailing zeros are being stripped before the check runs.

Targeting rule with empty property list matches all users
I created a feature flag rule and left the properties array empty in the targeting section. The configuration was accepted without any error, but the rule ended up applying to every user instead of filtering anyone out. I expected the system to reject an empty properties list or require at least one condition.

Predicate matching fails when numeric comparison values are sent as strings
When I define a targeting rule with a numeric operator like greater-than and send the threshold as a string instead of a number, the configuration is accepted but the resulting predicate does not match rules that use a bare number for the same comparison. Two targeting rules that should logically target the same population end up being treated as different because the value serialization differs between a string and a numeric input.

Retention period setting doesn't apply to performance event storage
When I try to update how long performance event data is kept, the configuration change appears to be ignored. The system generates an update query with a placeholder for the number of weeks, but the actual value never gets substituted in. I expected my custom retention period to take effect.

Materialized view creation fails with invalid column names
When deploying the system, the materialized view creation fails with a syntax error referencing an unexpected token in the column list. The generated column list contains entries that aren't actual column names—such as comment markers or directive words that precede the real column identifier on certain definition lines. The problem is in the logic that extracts column names from the column definition block.

Interactive component submissions fail with "no payload field" error
When users click buttons or select options from Slack modals in our workspace, the webhook delivery fails and the action never gets processed. The error indicates the payload field is missing from the form body. Regular message events and reactions work fine—only interactive components like buttons, menus, and modal submissions are affected. Submitting an empty response in Slack confirms the button renders and the click registers there, but our backend receives nothing.

Duplicate message processing
Identical Slack messages are being processed twice, causing duplicate downstream actions. The identifier assigned to each delivery is missing for some messages, so the system can't tell them apart from new ones. This happens intermittently with regular message events. I expected each message to be processed exactly once.

Batch session query returns wrong or empty results
When I request events for multiple sessions, the returned data doesn't match the sessions I asked for — sometimes it's empty, sometimes it includes events from unrelated sessions. The query runner seems to ignore my session ID filter entirely.

Column metadata does not match returned data in batch session queries
When a session batch query groups results by session, the column descriptions in the response are missing the session identifier column while the actual data rows still include it. Consumers reading the response columns to interpret the data rows get misaligned indices.

Constraint validation migration runs slowly on retries even when already complete
When I re-run a deployment after a failure, the constraint validation step takes much longer than expected because it modifies database timeout settings before checking whether the constraint has already been validated. On a retry where nothing needs to change, the operation still goes through the full setup process instead of skipping immediately.

NOT VALID ignored on constraint creation
I ran a migration to add a CHECK constraint, expecting it to be created in NOT VALID state so it wouldn't block writes while scanning existing rows. After the migration finished, the constraint was fully validated instead, which held up the table for much longer than expected.

Migration squashing crashes on constraint validation steps
Running the migration squashing command fails whenever a migration contains a step that validates a previously added constraint. Django can't resolve the operation class and crashes with an import error. I expect the squashing to succeed and produce a valid migration file.

Pagination drops the activity type filter
When I filter the running pipeline list to show only imports and click to the next page, the results switch back to showing all activity types. The page size and time window carry over, but the type filter is lost between pages.

Embedding generation hangs indefinitely when the service is slow
When I request an embedding synchronously, the call blocks forever if the embedding service takes too long to respond. The async variant times out after 30 seconds, but the synchronous version never does. I expected both to either complete or fail with a timeout rather than hanging forever.

Document embedding request rejected with invalid model error
When I submit a document for embedding, the operation fails with an error saying the model name is invalid, even though I believe I'm using a supported model. I was creating an embedding request for a document and expected it to be queued successfully. The error lists the allowed model names but doesn't explain why mine was rejected.

Documents not in the cache are silently dropped from results
When I request the recent emission times for a batch of documents, only the ones that have been processed show up in the response. I expected every document I asked about to appear in the result, with a null value for those that haven't been emitted yet. Because missing documents simply don't appear in the returned collection, downstream code that assumes all queried documents are present crashes with a key error.

Concurrent edits silently overwrite each other when both users make the same change
When two people edit the same feature flag at the same time and happen to set a field to the same value, no conflict error is raised. The second writer's changes go through without any warning, even though they were editing against stale data.

Duplicate-key error masks format validation
When I try to create a flag with a key that contains spaces and also matches another flag's key, the API returns a "key already exists" error. The format error about invalid characters never appears because the uniqueness check runs first and fails before the format check can run.

Sharing toggle shows as off even after enabling it
I enabled sharing on a dashboard and confirmed the setting was saved, but when I reload the page the sharing toggle appears disabled and shared links no longer work. It seems like the system only checks one sharing configuration and ignores the others.

Dashboard item count shows fewer items than I see on the page
When I check analytics for a dashboard, the reported item count is lower than the number of tiles actually displayed. Tiles that exist but haven't been populated with an insight yet are silently excluded from the count.

Trace spans not ingesting after deployment
After running migrations on the ClickHouse cluster, no new trace spans appear in the database even though Kafka is clearly receiving messages. The materialized view that bridges Kafka to the trace spans table maps incoming fields to the wrong columns — timestamps end up in kind slots, kind codes get stored as timestamps, and everything downstream is shifted. I expected all span metadata including kind, flags, and timestamps to be correctly populated when deploying.

Kafka metrics always show current time as last activity
The Kafka metrics dashboard always reports the most recent activity timestamp as right now, even when no new spans have arrived for hours. I expected it to reflect when the actual last span was received so I could tell if the ingestion pipeline had stalled.

Span attributes with long values silently missing from search
When I attach attributes with values over 256 characters to my spans, those attributes don't show up in the span attributes index or search results, even though the spans themselves are recorded normally. Shorter attributes on the same span appear fine. I expected all attributes to be searchable regardless of length.

API key 'Last used' timestamp doesn't update after making requests
When I use my personal API key multiple times within an hour, the 'Last used' time shown in its settings page stays the same instead of refreshing with each request. I expected it to reflect the most recent time the key was used.

Password-protected shared resources bypass organization public sharing restrictions
When an organization disables public sharing, non-password-protected shared links are blocked, but password-protected shared links remain accessible via their sharing access token. The organization-level restriction is only enforced for non-password-protected shares.

Boolean values accepted as team identifier
When sending webhook messages, boolean values like true or false are silently accepted as the team identifier instead of being rejected. Records end up assigned to teams 1 or 0 in the data warehouse, causing broken team-based queries and incorrect data segmentation.

Consumer crashes during Kafka group rebalances
When the webhook consumer loses its partitions during a rebalance, it tries to commit offsets after flushing its buffer. The commit fails because the partitions are no longer assigned, and the failure crashes the entire consumer process. I expected the consumer to gracefully hand off its work to another instance in the group.

Consumer crashes when dead-letter queue is unreachable
The consumer crashes entirely after encountering a malformed webhook message when the dead-letter queue topic is temporarily unreachable. I expected the system to log the failure and continue processing subsequent messages, but the entire consumer process exits instead.

Push token registration fails when re-registering the same device
When I reinstall the app and try to enable push notifications again, the registration silently fails and I never receive any notifications. This happens because my device already has a registered token from before the reinstall. I expected the system to update the existing token's last-seen timestamp rather than rejecting the duplicate registration.

Detailed error messages hidden for provider and configuration failures
When an evaluation fails because of an API key issue or provider problem, I only see a short summary message. I'd expect to see the full underlying error message like I do when my custom evaluation code crashes. Without that detail, I can't tell if it's a timeout, authentication error, or something else.

Error messages are silently cut off in the dashboard
When an evaluation fails with a long error message, only the first 2000 characters appear and the rest is hidden behind an ellipsis. I lost important context about what went wrong and had to dig into logs to find the full message.

Model not found error silently ignored for managed providers
When the selected model is no longer available while using a managed provider, the evaluation fails without any user-friendly error message. The same situation works fine with a bring-your-own-key provider, where the model not found error is properly surfaced.

Spike notification shows "inf" multiplier when baseline is zero
When an error tracking issue spikes but the historical baseline count is zero, the notification displays "inf over baseline" instead of a meaningful comparison. This makes the alert confusing and unhelpful for understanding the severity of the spike.

Minimum edge weight of 0 is silently ignored
When I set the minimum edge weight filter to 0 to include all edges regardless of weight, the filter appears to have no effect and behaves as if it were unset. Setting it to any positive number works fine. I expected that a value of 0 would be accepted as a valid minimum threshold.

Maximum edge weight ignored when set to zero
When I set the maximum edge weight filter to zero on a paths query, it has no effect and the system behaves as if no limit was specified. I expected zero to be a valid value that excludes all edges with any positive weight.

Aggregate raw diff count inflated with excluded members
The cohort comparison summary reports a higher total raw difference than expected. It appears to include members that were deliberately excluded from the diff because the new pipeline hasn't emitted decisions for them yet. When comparing the aggregate numbers against individual cohort results, the total doesn't add up.

Fallback counter reports success even when shared table returns no data
When the dedicated AI events table has no matching records and the system falls back to the shared events table, the monitoring counter marks the query as a successful fallback regardless of whether the second attempt actually found any rows. Dashboards then show fallback queries as succeeding even when both tables came up empty.

AI events table still queried after disabling the feature flag
After turning off the AI events table rollout flag for our organization, queries for AI events still attempt to read from the dedicated table instead of falling back to the shared events table. I expected the kill switch to immediately route all AI events queries away from the dedicated table.

Data model materialization fails with timeout errors for larger models
When I trigger a materialization on a data model that has many source rows, the process fails with a timeout error even though the same model works fine when run through the alternative query engine. Smaller models complete without issue. I expected all models to be able to finish regardless of how many rows they need to process.

Job stays marked as failed after successful retry
When a data model materialization job fails and is retried, the dashboard still shows it as failed even though the retry completed successfully. The status never updates to reflect the new outcome.

Trino model run state never recorded without incremental config
After a managed warehouse model completes successfully through Trino, the incremental state is never updated if the saved query lacks an incremental configuration. This means subsequent runs cannot determine whether the model was previously materialized, causing unnecessary full refreshes every time.

Impersonation tokens persist after staff logout
When a staff member logs out from an impersonation session, the impersonated user's OAuth access tokens remain valid and continue to work. We expected all tokens created during the impersonation to be revoked when the admin disconnects.

Revoking all sessions for an OAuth application doesn't immediately block active connections
When an admin revokes every session for a connected app, a user who happens to be refreshing their token at that exact moment can still get a new access token that bypasses the revocation. The admin expects all sessions to be invalidated instantly, but the concurrent refresh slips through and creates a valid token after the sweep completes.

Refresh tokens still appear active after revoking all app sessions
After using the "revoke all sessions" button for an OAuth application, querying for my user's live refresh tokens still returns those tokens. They don't work for actual token exchange, but the listing shows them as active. I expected the live token query to respect application-level session revocation and exclude those tokens.

The live refresh token query only checks individual token revocation status and doesn't consider the application's session revocation timestamp.

Custom separator ignored for parent segments
When I parse a fully qualified name with a custom separator, only the final table name is extracted correctly. Parent segments stay joined together instead of being split into individual hierarchy levels.

Compatibility check allows invalid type conversions
Batch exports fail mid-pipeline when converting a timestamp field to an integer, even though the system confirmed the types were compatible before starting. The conversion produces garbled values instead of valid integers, causing the entire export to abort. I expected the system to either reject the incompatible types upfront or perform the conversion correctly.

Field cannot be updated by alias
When I try to update a field using its alias as the key, I get an error saying the field name doesn't match, even though the field exists and I can retrieve it using the same alias. I expected to be able to update fields by their name or alias, consistent with how I can read them.

Shutdown callback silently skipped in synchronous mode
I registered a cleanup callback with the shutdown monitor, expecting it to execute when the worker begins shutting down. But when using the synchronous context manager, the callback is silently skipped and never runs. I expected the callback to fire regardless of whether I use the async or sync version of the context manager.

Retryable shutdown error becomes a runtime error
During graceful worker shutdown, activities fail with a generic runtime error instead of the expected retryable shutdown error. This happens when the shutdown notification is raised but the activity context is no longer available, preventing proper retries.

Shutdown signal takes a full second to register
When the orchestrator sends a termination signal, the worker doesn't start cleaning up until about a second later. I was scaling down a pod and noticed the shutdown wasn't immediate even though the signal was received. I expected the worker to begin its graceful shutdown almost right away.

Query row limit silently capped during execution
When I set a high row limit on my query, the system silently reduces it without any warning. My results contain fewer rows than I asked for, and there's no indication that the limit was changed. Lower limits work as expected, but once I go above a certain threshold, my query is silently truncated.

Metrics server stays alive after worker crashes
When a worker task fails and the process exits, the metrics HTTP server that was started alongside it keeps running in the background, holding onto its port and consuming memory. I expected the metrics endpoint to shut down together with the worker so resources are fully reclaimed.

Histogram bucket overrides silently dropped for certain task queues
We deployed a worker for a new task queue type and noticed the latency histograms use default bucket ranges instead of the custom ones we configured. Other task queues show the expected buckets, but this one falls back to the defaults. We expected the worker setup to apply the appropriate histogram bucket overrides for all recognized task queues.

JSON length returns null for object values
Measuring the length of a JSON field returns null whenever the value is an object, though arrays work fine and return the correct count. I expected the same behavior for both types.

Random function ignores seed argument
When I pass a seed value to the random number function to get reproducible results, the seed is silently ignored and each query returns different random values. I expected the function to respect the seed for consistent results across runs.

Raw JSON extraction returns variant type instead of text
When extracting raw JSON content from a field, the result comes back as a structured variant instead of plain text. This causes type errors when the extracted value is used in string operations like concatenation or comparison. Other JSON extraction functions correctly return strings, making this behavior inconsistent and unexpected.

Local S3 queries for web analytics always hit the wrong bucket
When I run locally, queries for web analytics data always target a hardcoded bucket name rather than using the same bucket configured for production. If I change the production bucket, my local environment keeps pointing at the old one and fails. The local URL construction should respect the production bucket setting.

S3 web stats export missing dimension columns
When I query the daily web analytics S3 export table, I only get period bucket, team ID, and raw aggregate counts — no hostname, device type, page path, or geographic data. The regular in-app web analytics table shows all those dimensions, so I expected the S3 export to include them too. Without them I can't break down traffic by browser, country, or referring source.

Web bounces table returns no data
When I query the web bounces analytics table built from S3, it returns zero rows even though I can see pageviews in the regular stats table. The bounces and session duration columns are missing from the results entirely. I expected the bounces table to show bounce counts and session durations alongside the standard metrics.

Bulk embedding insert crashes on empty input
Calling the bulk embedding creation function with an empty list still attempts to run an INSERT statement with no values, which causes a database syntax error. I expected the function to handle empty input gracefully and simply do nothing.

Removal count inflated in activity log
Moving an insight between dashboards sometimes logs more removals than I made. If an insight was previously removed from a dashboard and later re-added, removing it again records an extra removal for the old dashboard alongside the actual one.

Restored insight reappears on dashboards it was removed from
When I restore a deleted insight, it shows up again on dashboards I had previously removed it from. I expected restoring an insight to only bring back its original placement, not resurrect tiles I'd intentionally taken off dashboards.

Tiles created on unexpected dashboards
When placing an insight on multiple dashboards at once, the tiles sometimes end up on dashboards that weren't in the original request. I pass a list of dashboard IDs, get back a placement plan, and then apply it — but the resulting tiles include dashboards I never asked for. I expected the placement to only touch the dashboards I specified.

title: Tiles created on unexpected dashboards
body: When placing an insight on multiple dashboards at once, the tiles sometimes end up on dashboards that weren't in the original request. I pass a list of dashboard IDs, get back a placement plan, and then apply it — but the resulting tiles include dashboards I never asked for. I expected the placement to only touch the dashboards I specified.

Async views losing session data
I have an async view that modifies session data, but the changes don't stick. After the request completes, the session data is back to its original state. Regular sync views work fine.

Newly created sessions missing activity timestamp
Sessions created through the async path don't have a last activity timestamp set, showing as blank in the admin panel. Sessions created through the synchronous path work fine. I expected all newly created sessions to have an activity timestamp recorded.

Logged-in user's session loses its user ID
After logging in, subsequent requests treat the session as anonymous. Page views and events stop being attributed to my account and show up under 'Anonymous' instead. Relogging fixes it temporarily, but the problem returns on the next session. The session data still contains my authentication credentials.

Custom integrations disappear after running the template sync command
After running the template synchronization command, several of my custom integrations vanished from the interface. They had been working properly before, but the sync process removed them even though they should still be active. I expected the command to update existing templates without deleting any that are still in use.

Logs queries ignore property groups setting
When running a logs query with property groups explicitly disabled, the query still uses optimized property groups anyway. The configuration I set has no effect for logs workloads — it gets silently overridden. I expected my explicit setting to be respected like it is for other query types.

Password rejected after being entered exactly as provided
I received a newly generated password from my colleague to access a shared dashboard. I copied the password character for character into the prompt, but every attempt was denied. Refreshing the page and trying again produced the same result. Other passwords for different shared resources work without issue.

Password update doesn't persist after changing it
When I update the password for a shared dashboard, the change appears to go through, but after refreshing the page the old password still works. I have to create an entirely new password entry instead of being able to modify the existing one.

Digest remains enabled for other organizations
I disabled the error tracking digest for a user by providing their email along with an organization ID. The user stopped receiving digests for that organization's projects, but they still receive digests for projects in other organizations they belong to. I expected the digest to be fully disabled for the user.

Digest disable preview shows inflated project count
When previewing changes before applying the bulk digest disable for an organization, the tool says it will disable the digest for every project in the org. But some users already have it turned off for certain projects, so fewer changes will actually be made. The preview count is higher than reality.

Overlapping regex filters produce empty results
When I add a regex filter and a not-regex filter on the same property, the system only flags them as conflicting if the two patterns are character-for-character identical. If the excluded pattern covers everything the first filter would match, the filters are treated as compatible and the query returns no results.

Null entries in value arrays become the literal text "None"
When a property filter includes null inside its value array, it gets turned into the string "None" instead of being skipped. This makes the filter match against the literal word None and can cause false conflicts with other filters on the same property.

LLM signal exceeds token limit
I noticed that some error tracking signals sent to the LLM are being rejected due to exceeding the maximum token length. The signal should be trimmed before sending, but it appears the token counting and the trimming use different encodings, so the final trimmed message can still go over the limit.

I was looking at error reports where the signal was delivered but the LLM returned an error about input length. I expected all signals to stay within the configured token budget.

Copying a resource produces '(Copy 2)' even when '(Copy 1)' is available
When I duplicate a resource whose name already exists in the destination team, the system sometimes skips '(Copy 1)' and assigns '(Copy 2)' instead. This happens whenever a bare '(Copy)' suffix is already taken — the deduplication logic then starts checking numbered copies from two and never considers one.

Folded record count exceeds unique memberships in output state
After running a reconciliation fold, the number of folded records is higher than the total unique person-cohort pairs in the resulting state. Replayed messages with older timestamps pass validation and are counted as folded even though they're silently ignored because a newer record is already present. I expected the folded count to match the actual number of records in the output.

Timestamp parsing rejects valid values with trailing whitespace
Valid records are being silently dropped during the fold because their timestamps include trailing whitespace that prevents the parsing step from recognizing them. The timestamps are otherwise correct, but the parsing doesn't trim the whitespace before matching. The drop count for unrecognized records is higher than expected, and the issue affects a consistent subset of records.

Completeness flag never reports true
Even after all partitions have been recorded for a reconcile run, the completeness check still returns false. I expected it to confirm completion once every partition has been seen.

Conditional lazy field access breaks when field is in the else branch
I'm querying with an if expression that conditionally accesses a field from a related table — something like checking a status and returning a field from the joined table in both branches. When the lazy-joined field appears in the else branch of the if, the query fails as if that table was never joined. It works fine when the field is only in the true/then branch. I expected both branches to resolve correctly since the join should be added regardless of which branch uses the field.

Wrapped lazy table subquery fails with unknown column error
When a lazy table gets wrapped in a subquery due to circular dependencies, the subquery tries to select internal tracking identifiers as column names instead of actual field names. Queries fail with an unknown column error when accessing properties on these lazy tables.

Properties on lazy tables silently dropped in non-standard query flows
When accessing properties on lazy tables from non-standard query entry points, the properties are silently skipped during resolution. Regular field accesses on the same lazy tables work fine, but property-based access fails. This prevents building reports and dashboards that rely on lazy table properties through alternative query paths.

Deprecation warning not shown for feature flag events in subqueries
My query compared the event column to the feature flag called event inside a subquery, but I never received the deprecation warning about migrating to the flag evaluations table. The query ran without any warnings and only after reading documentation did I learn the pattern would stop working.

Migration warning missing for exclusion queries
When I exclude the feature flag called event from my results using a NOT IN clause, I don't see the migration warning. But when I include it with IN, the warning appears. I expected to see the warning regardless of whether I'm including or excluding the event.

Deprecation warning missing when query uses a saved view
My query references a saved view that filters on feature flag events, but I never see the deprecation warning telling me to migrate. The warning does show up on similar queries that don't use a saved view. I expected to be warned either way so I could update my queries before the old table is removed.

Newly created web experiments don't appear in my web experiments list

Command generates new tokens when existing valid access token is still usable
I ran the token generation command without the force flag, expecting it to reuse my existing valid tokens. Instead it created a completely fresh set. My access token hadn't expired, but the refresh token had been revoked by a cleanup job. I expected the command to detect the still-valid access token and reuse it rather than regenerating everything.

Token generation fails after deleting old OAuth application
After deleting my Stripe OAuth application from the database and running the token generation command again, it failed with an error saying the configured client ID doesn't match any application. I expected the command to detect that the old app was gone and create a new one automatically.

Exposure count stuck at zero for healthy experiments
The experiment dashboard shows zero total exposures even though the experiment has been receiving traffic. The count stays at zero until the next scheduled cycle.

Experiment metrics stuck after a failed recalculation
After a manual recalculation finishes with errors, the next hourly scheduled run is silently skipped and the dashboard still shows old values. It takes up to an hour before fresh data appears again. I expected any new scheduled run to override a stale or broken result rather than being blocked by it.

Admin pagination shows thousands of pages even with few records
When browsing the admin interface, the pagination bar displays an absurdly large number of pages (thousands) even though the table contains only a handful of records. This makes navigation unusable because the page selector is filled with irrelevant page numbers. I expected it to show only the actual number of pages needed for the visible records.

Slot acquisition return value is ambiguous
When trying to acquire a slot for an evaluation check, the function returns None without explaining why. I can't tell if the alert wasn't admitted or if the system is at capacity. The documentation only mentions the capacity case, so I don't know how to recover.

Alert evaluations stop running after extended periods
After my alerts run for several hours, they begin to fail silently and no evaluations execute at all. Restarting the service temporarily fixes the problem, but it always comes back. I expected evaluation slots to be released automatically when each check finishes so that alerts would keep running continuously without manual intervention.

Sync schedule fires at wrong time when sync frequency is shorter than the configured time of day
I set my data sync to run at 3:00 AM with an hourly frequency, but the jobs start running at midnight instead. The scheduled time of day is ignored whenever the sync frequency is shorter than the number of minutes from midnight to the configured time.

Scheduled syncs fire at the wrong time of day
When I configure an external data source to sync at 3 PM, the actual syncs fire at 6 PM instead. The configured sync time is shifted forward and the schedule never runs at the time I set. I expected the sync to honour the exact time I configured.

CDC extraction schedule creation fails when schedule already exists
When I run the CDC extraction schedule setup for a source that already has an active schedule, the operation throws an error instead of updating the existing one. The documentation says it should create or update, so running it a second time should succeed.

Duplicate billing records persist across days despite resends
When a producer corrects a billing record by resending it with updated data, the correction only takes effect if it arrives on the same calendar day as the original. Resends on a different day create a new duplicate entry instead of replacing the old one. I expected every resend of the same record to overwrite the previous version regardless of when it arrived.

Corrected billing quantities persist alongside originals
When a usage producer corrects a previously reported quantity, both the old and new values appear in my billing totals instead of the corrected one replacing the original. I resend the same record with the right amount, but the system keeps the first version I sent.

Migration tool crashes when bridging from legacy migration system
When transitioning from a previous migration system that used its own tracking table, the command crashes with a database error claiming the legacy tracking table doesn't exist, even though the table is present. This happens during the bridge phase when the command tries to check which migrations were already applied by the old system. Instead of crashing, the command should fall back to treating all migrations as new and continuing normally.

Migration refused due to unrelated invalid index
When I try to apply a migration that creates an index concurrently, the command refuses to proceed because it finds an invalid index with the same name in a different schema. The invalid index is from a previous migration in a different schema and has nothing to do with the current migration. I have to manually drop the unrelated index before I can proceed.

Migration doesn't detect broken index from interrupted run
I ran a migration that creates an index concurrently. A previous run was interrupted, leaving an invalid index behind, but the migration didn't catch it and proceeded anyway. Now the query planner sometimes picks the wrong index and performance is degraded. I expected the migration to refuse to run and tell me how to drop the broken index.

Cooldown expires mid-send
When I configure an alert with a cooldown period, two initial notification messages sometimes appear within seconds of each other instead of being properly spaced apart. The first message begins sending but hasn't finished when a second message gets through and posts its own initial notification anyway.

I expected the cooldown setting to reliably prevent any new initial notifications from being delivered for the full duration, no matter how long the first one takes to send.

Root message status gets updated on every reply
When an alert thread has multiple replies, the root message's status line keeps getting rechecked and edited even for non-status events like new errors or comments. I expected only actual status transitions to update the root message, but every single reply triggers a status check that can produce another edit, clutters the thread with redundant updates, and adds unnecessary database lookups on each reply.

Error message shows raw array brackets instead of readable text
When I submit an experiment with invalid settings, the error sometimes displays as square brackets like [] instead of actual text explaining what's wrong. I expected to see a clear description of the configuration problem.

Unexpected technical error shown to users
When an experiment metric calculation fails with an uncommon or unexpected error type, the frontend displays a raw technical exception instead of a friendly message. For example, after a transient database issue, the page showed a low-level stack trace rather than a clear explanation. I expected every failure to produce a readable error message, since this module is supposed to centralize user-friendly error handling for experiments.

Census crashes evaluating teams with no direct scans
The enrollment census crashes when a team has zero direct-scan metric reads in the evaluation window. The crash occurs during the slow read percentage calculation, which divides by the total number of direct reads. This prevents the entire census from completing and blocks enrollment for all teams.

Precompute enrollment undercounts running metrics
When I check the enrollment report, my team shows fewer running metrics than I expect based on all the scheduled metrics I've set up. The enrollment logic only counts scheduled metrics attached to individual experiments, completely missing metrics defined at the team level.

Enrollment doesn't fully roll back on failure
When enrollment fails partway through, the teams already processed stay enrolled instead of being undone. Running the census again adds more teams on top of the partial batch instead of starting fresh.

Command crashes with invalid team ID input
When I run the migration command with --team-ids and accidentally include a non-numeric value like a typo or extra character, the entire command crashes with an unhandled exception instead of showing a helpful error message. I expected the command to validate the comma-separated list and tell me which value is invalid.

Person property values sometimes show unexpected formatting
When viewing person property values in autocomplete suggestions, some entries appear garbled or duplicated. The result formatter tries to parse every value as JSON regardless of type, and when the input isn't a string, the parsing error is silently suppressed and the value is passed through in an incorrect format.

Array property values split into multiple suggestions
When I look up a person or event property that has an array value stored as JSON, each element appears as its own suggestion instead of the full array. For example, if I set a tag property to ["urgent", "review"], the autocomplete shows "urgent" and "review" as separate options rather than showing the combined value as one entry. I expected to see the original array value as a single suggestion.

Deleting an already-removed release returns not found instead of success
When I try to delete a release that no longer exists, the API returns a not found error. I expected the delete operation to succeed silently, since the resource is already gone. This makes it difficult to write idempotent deletion scripts.

Update returns content in no-content response
When I update a release, the response includes a body even though the status is 204 No Content. Some HTTP clients reject responses with bodies on 204 status codes.

Hash id length check says bytes but measures characters
When submitting a hash id containing multi-byte Unicode characters, the system reports that the length cannot exceed 128 bytes, but the actual validation counts characters rather than bytes. A hash with 128 multi-byte characters passes through even though its encoded form exceeds 128 bytes.

Spike event cleanup workflow fails when triggered with an empty input
When I run the spike event cleanup task from the admin interface without specifying any parameters, it crashes with a JSON parsing error instead of running with the default retention period. I expected it to clean up events older than thirty days like it normally does.

Some users don't receive materialization failure notifications even though they have access to the data model
A teammate with full access to our project didn't get a materialization failure alert for a data model they can open in the UI without any issues. Other members with similar access levels received the notification just fine. The model had clearly been failing and needed attention — they simply weren't told. I expected everyone who can access the data model to be notified when it breaks.

Schema selection ignores later modifier changes
After changing query modifiers mid-query, the events schema still reflects the original configuration instead of the updated one. I expected that modifying the modifiers would take effect on subsequent calls within the same context.

Resource reference tags return null instead of empty arrays
When a query doesn't reference any saved queries, warehouse tables, or direct reads, the resource tags come back as null instead of empty arrays. Downstream tools that expect arrays and try to iterate over the values will crash.

Sensitive values can overwrite regular values in query parameters
When building a query that needs both regular and sensitive parameter values, the wrong value sometimes gets substituted during execution. This happens intermittently — if I add a regular value first, then a sensitive one, then another regular value, the third value ends up replacing the sensitive one in the final query. The result is that the query returns incorrect data or exposes sensitive information under a non-sensitive placeholder.

Expected behavior: each parameter value gets a unique placeholder regardless of whether it was added via the regular or sensitive path.

Symbol set never gets linked to its release after bulk upload
I uploaded symbol sets for a new release, but when I check the dashboard the symbol sets show up without any release association. The upload completes successfully and the source maps are there, yet the release binding step appears to have been skipped. If I re-upload the same chunks with the release ID included, they still don't get linked. I expected the bulk upload process to associate existing orphaned symbol sets with the release they were shipped in.

Symbol sets are being deleted while still actively deployed
I upload a new release with unchanged source maps, but after some time the symbol sets disappear from the UI and exceptions can no longer be symbolicated. The chunks haven't changed between deploys, so the rows should persist indefinitely. They get removed as if they were abandoned, even though they're still in active use across multiple releases.

Array contains filter returns false positives
When I filter activity logs by an array field using the contains operation, the results include records where the search term appears as a substring anywhere in the JSON detail field, not just inside the specified array. For example, searching for a change type like "button" also matches records where "button" appears as part of another word or in a completely different field. I expected the filter to only match when the value actually exists as an element in the target array.

Exact filter on array field returns partial matches
When I filter activity logs for an exact value in a simple array field like changes[], entries containing a substring of my search value are returned instead of only exact matches. For example, searching for "update" also returns entries where the array contains "updated". I expected exact matching to return only items that match the full value precisely.

Issue description changes don't appear in activity history
When I edit an issue's description and save it, the change doesn't show up in the activity history. Other fields like status and name are recorded correctly, but description edits are invisible in the audit trail even though the new text is saved.

Splitting an issue sometimes leaves no trace in the activity log
When I split an issue, it divides correctly but the action doesn't show up in my team's activity history. Other mutations like merging or updating always appear there. This makes it hard to audit who split what and when.

Assignment email sent even when assignment fails to save
When I assign an issue to someone, the assigned person sometimes receives an email notification but the assignment doesn't actually stick — reloading the page shows no assignee. This seems to happen intermittently, suggesting a race condition.

Expected: the email should only be sent if the assignment is successfully saved.

Workflow silently uses team ID 0 when no input is given
When I trigger the daily intent clustering without specifying any parameters, it completes successfully but returns results for team ID 0 instead of failing or prompting for a team. I expected either an error asking me to specify a team or at least a warning in the logs.

Skipped reports sometimes lack an explanation
When a count-triggered evaluation wasn't triggered because the result count hadn't reached the threshold yet, the response showed the report as not due but gave no reason. Monitoring couldn't distinguish between reports skipped due to cooldowns or daily caps and those simply waiting for more data.

Report says completed but has no sections or metrics
After triggering an evaluation report, the generation finishes successfully but the resulting report contains no analysis — no sections, no citations, no metrics. It looks like a blank report that was labeled as done. I expected either actual findings in the report or a clear indication that nothing could be generated rather than a completed status with empty content.

Report prompt guidance always empty
When I configure an evaluation with custom prompt guidance, the guidance doesn't appear in the generated report context. It comes through blank every time regardless of what I set. I expected my guidance text to be included so the agent knows how to structure the report.

Backfill progress counter freezes midway through evaluation window
I launched a backfill evaluation across a multi-day date range and watched the dispatched count increase normally for the first several batches. Then the counter suddenly stopped advancing even though the backfill continued running. The evaluation row remained in an active state indefinitely, preventing any subsequent backfill from starting. I expected the progress to continue until all eligible units were evaluated.

Duplicate evaluations fire during reruns
When I trigger a rerun of an existing evaluation, I see some units being evaluated twice — once by the original live ingestion and again by the backfill. The two runs overlap in time instead of the backfill waiting for the live one to finish.

Backfill settle window extends beyond configured value
When I set a settle time for session evaluations, the backfill still holds back items that have been settled for longer than my setting. The settle window shown in the interface doesn't match what the backfill actually uses — items become eligible for backfill later than expected.

Async query status endpoint returns 400 for internal server errors
When I check the status of a failed async query, the API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request even though the failure was caused by a system-side issue, not my request. The error response includes a message describing the internal failure, so it's clear the query itself was fine. I expected a 500 Internal Server Error for infrastructure problems, which would tell me to retry later rather than fix my query.

Query log endpoint returns nothing for queries run today
The API docs say I can retrieve query logs for queries issued within the last 24 hours, but when I run a query and immediately try to fetch its log, I get an empty result. Queries from previous days show up fine. I expected to be able to look up the log for any recent query regardless of whether it was run today or yesterday.

Async auth check always succeeds regardless of credentials
The async authentication check endpoint returns success for every request, even without valid credentials. This makes it useless for verifying whether a token or session is still valid before starting an async query.

Page crashes when integration lookup fails for non-budget reasons
Loading a page that displays ownership attribution sometimes crashes with an unhandled error instead of falling back to anonymous access. The crash occurs when the system tries to find a GitHub App installation that can read a repository - if the lookup fails for reasons other than a budget or rate limit issue, the error propagates up rather than degrading gracefully. I expected the page to always show ownership information, with anonymous read as a fallback.

Sluggish performance after a force push persists for hours
After someone force-pushed to our main branch, checking out ownership on our team's repository became noticeably slow. Even after normal commits restored things, the slowdown lasted for many hours before gradually improving. I expected the performance to recover within minutes once the repository was back to a normal state.

Deletion verification never marks records as confirmed
After triggering a bulk data deletion, the initial processing step completes but the follow-up verification leaves everything stuck in a pending state. Nothing transitions to confirmed even though the underlying data has been removed. I expected the system to confirm deletions once verification ran.

Deletion process stops after first batch failure
When I submitted a large batch of deletions, the process started but stopped partway through after encountering bad data in one chunk. The remaining deletions were left unprocessed and stayed in a pending state.

Bulk data deletion only removes the last item
When I trigger a deletion for multiple teams or entities at once, only the last one actually gets deleted. The earlier ones appear untouched after the job completes. I expected all of them to be removed since they were queued together.

Verification of deletions shows the same pattern—only the final entity's verification condition is checked, so previously-deleted items may incorrectly remain marked as verified.

Plugin server health metrics show misspelled names
When I check the instance status dashboard, the plugin server alive and job queue metrics are labeled with 'plugin sever' instead of 'plugin server'. The typo makes these entries confusing during system health reviews and breaks any scripts that filter or search for the correct metric names.

Person/session data merge fails for records with certain Unicode characters
When batch exporting person or session data to BigQuery, the merge step fails intermittently for records containing specific Unicode characters in JSON fields. Direct inserts of the same data work fine. The issue appears only when the system needs to merge stage tables into a final table (e.g. for mutable models like persons or sessions), not for simple append-only event exports.

I expected all records to merge successfully regardless of which Unicode characters they contain.

Missing baseline comparison in spike alerts
When an issue starts spiking, the Slack notification says "5 events in the last window, no baseline yet" even though the issue has been accumulating errors for weeks. I expected to see a comparison like "5 events in the last window vs baseline 2" since there is plenty of historical data to compare against.

Spiking alert omits event count
When an issue starts spiking, the reply sometimes just says "Spiking again" without showing how many events are involved. I was expecting to see the current count compared to the baseline, but the summary is missing even though the issue is definitely spiking.

Alert headline disappears after editing
When I edit a root alert message in Slack, the response payload is missing the headline field that the original message had. Downstream integrations that read the headline from any message object crash on edited ones.

Steps funnel with breakdown shows only one series per step instead of one per breakdown value
When I create a funnel alert using a steps visualization with a breakdown, the evaluation returns fewer series than expected — for a 2-step funnel with 3 breakdown values, I get 2 series instead of 3. Each series is labeled with the first step's breakdown value, and the conversion rate calculation only considers the steps within each group rather than grouping all steps by their breakdown value.

Single-step funnel with conversion from previous saves but fails at evaluation
I created a funnel alert with a single step and selected conversion from previous step as the metric. The alert saved without error, but when it evaluated, it crashed saying conversion from previous is undefined at the first step. Switching to conversion from start made it work.

Conversion rate drops spuriously when only one period of data exists
Funnel alerts with historical trends show a sudden drop in conversion rate when there is only one period in the data range, even though nothing has actually changed. The alert evaluates against the incomplete current period instead of treating it as insufficient data.

Lag feature function returns wrong array shape when no lags are requested
The documentation states that creating lag features always produces a 2D array, but when zero lag features are requested, it returns the original 1D time series instead. This breaks downstream code that expects consistent 2D output regardless of the lag count.

Sample percent produces biased results
When I run the management command with --sample-percent set below 100, the selected alerts seem to cluster around certain ID ranges instead of being evenly spread. For example, with 50% the same subset always gets picked on every run, and those alerts tend to have sequential or similarly-patterned IDs. I expected the sample to be more representative of the full alert population.

S3 offload silently drops uploads under burst traffic
During traffic spikes our Redis memory kept climbing even though S3 offload was enabled for our organization. Cache entries that should have been moved to S3 stayed in Redis instead. After the spike passed the uploads resumed normally. I expected the offload mechanism to handle burst traffic rather than silently dropping uploads.

Web vitals path breakdown shows inflated values after re-running precomputation
After re-running a precomputation job for web vitals, the path breakdown metrics show inflated values compared to a fresh computation. The old job's data and the new job's data both appear in query results, causing duplicate entries for the same paths.

Web vitals queries become very slow over time
As more data accumulates, queries for web vitals metrics take progressively longer to complete. Some backend nodes handle most of the data while others stay nearly empty, causing uneven load and degraded performance for dashboard loading.

Scoring summary counts include results from failed partition batches
After running the session replay scoring workflow, the final tally shows more sessions scored than expected. Some partition batches failed during processing, but their partial results were still added to the overall count. I expected the summary to only reflect sessions from batches that completed successfully.

Scored session count exceeds fetched count
When I check the results of the scoring job, the number of scored sessions is sometimes higher than the number of fetched sessions for the same chunk. This doesn't make sense since we should only be able to score what we've fetched. I expected scored to never exceed fetched.

Funnel alert evaluates incomplete data buckets
I set up a funnel alert with a minimum threshold and a fast check schedule, but it keeps triggering on data that hasn't fully accumulated yet. When I tried the same pattern with a trend alert, the system refused to save it unless I added a maximum threshold. I expected funnel alerts to have the same protection against evaluating partial time periods.

Notebook widget save fails even with valid inputs
I configured a notebook widget by selecting both the source notebook and a widget snapshot, but the save fails with an error telling me to provide both fields. I verified that both fields contain valid values, so the rejection seems incorrect.

Role assignee filter rejects valid short identifiers
When I try to filter recent tickets by a role assignee, the request fails saying the role identifier must be a UUID. I'm using the short code shown in the role settings, which is how all other role references work in the product.

Priority filter gives no details on invalid values
When I filter conversation tickets by priority and include an invalid priority, the API returns a generic error without telling me which priorities are invalid. I have to guess which of my selected priorities is wrong instead of getting a clear list of rejected values.

Pre-aggregated web vitals table ignores query context
When querying the pre-aggregated web vitals table through HogQL, the underlying ClickHouse table selection does not respect the query context. I noticed that passing different query settings or contexts has no effect on which table is used — the same distributed table is always returned regardless of context. I expected the context to allow selecting between different table variants (for example, a local vs. distributed table depending on the query settings).

Usage metric timestamps are always in UTC
The timestamps on my usage metrics appear to be in UTC even though my team is set to a different timezone. I expected the timestamps to reflect my team's local timezone.
